newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Patten pledges support for post-1997 leader.
newsitem.headline: HK's Patten pledges support for post-1997 leader.

text.p: Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten pledged on Wednesday to support Hong Kong's first post-colonial leader.
The British colony reverts to China at midnight on June 30, 1997, and becomes a Special Administrative Region of China governed by a Chief Executive.

"The first Chief Executive can certainly count on my support and good wishes both before and after the first of July next year," Patten told the Legislative Council in his annual policy speech, the last by a British governor.
"We in Hong Kong will want the Chief Executive to succeed because we want the transition to succeed. To succeed triumphantly. How could we want anything else?" he said.
"I want, we all want, Hong Kong to do better in the future after 1997.." he said before going on to paint a rosy picture of Hong Kong's potential of becoming the "New York of Asia".
